sectionsContent.title: Projectile Motion, Part 3: Full Projectile Motion

concept.summary: Every projectile problem is the same two motions sharing one clock: constant velocity sideways, free fall up and down. In the full version the landing can be higher or lower than the launch, and the launch can point up, down, or level. Without a symmetric path there is no half-time shortcut. Solve the vertical equation for the time directly, which usually takes the quadratic formula.
keyIdeas: y is the landing height measured from the launch point: negative below it, positive above it.
The quadratic gives two times. Keep the one that makes physical sense. A landing on the way down is the larger positive time.

items: Components of the launch velocity, with the calculator in degree mode (Part 2).
Horizontal velocity never changes in the air; vertical velocity changes by 9.8 m/s every second (Parts 1 and 2).
Rebuilding a vector from its components: magnitude with the Pythagorean theorem, angle with inverse tangent (S2.2).

sectionsContent.directions: Work every problem in your Hayden-McNeil notebook. Sketch the path, mark the launch point as the origin, and label the landing height. Up is +y and the direction of launch is +x, so g = −9.8 m/s². A launch below the horizontal has a negative vy0. When you use the quadratic formula, say which of the two times you kept and why. Ignore air resistance. Round answers to the correct number of significant figures; g = 9.8 m/s² has two.

questions.prompt: Captain Jack Sparrow's crew fires a cannonball at 22 m/s, 25° above the horizontal, from a clifftop fort 18 m above the sea. Jack insists he was aiming at that rock. Find the time the cannonball takes to hit the water and how far from the base of the cliff it lands.
questions.solution:
vx = 22 cos 25° = 19.94 m/s. vy0 = 22 sin 25° = 9.30 m/s. The water is 18 m below the launch, so y = −18 m.
−18 = 9.30t + ½(−9.8)t², so 4.9t² − 9.30t − 18 = 0.
t = [9.30 + √(9.30² + 4(4.9)(18))] / 2(4.9) = (9.30 + 20.96) / 9.8 = 3.09 s, which is 3.1 s. The other root is negative and is thrown out.
x = vx·t = (19.94)(3.09) = 61.6 m, which is 62 m.

steps.note: the water is below the launch, so y is negative

questions.prompt: Link fires an arrow at 45 m/s, 10° above the horizontal, at a target 62 m away horizontally. The Bokoblin holding the target has made some poor choices. Find the time the arrow takes to reach the target and how far above or below the launch height it hits.
questions.solution:
vx = 45 cos 10° = 44.32 m/s. vy0 = 45 sin 10° = 7.81 m/s.
The horizontal distance gives the time: t = 62 / 44.32 = 1.399 s, which is 1.4 s.
y = (7.81)(1.399) + ½(−9.8)(1.399)² = 1.34 m. Positive, so the arrow hits 1.3 m above the launch height.
questions.finalAnswer: t = 1.4 s (1.399 s)   y = 1.3 m above launch height (1.34 m)

questions.prompt: Michelangelo tosses a pizza box at 14 m/s, 60° above the horizontal, up onto a rooftop 6.0 m above his hand. It lands on the roof on its way down. Leonardo suggested the stairs. Find the time until the box lands on the roof and the horizontal distance it travels.
questions.solution:
vx = 14 cos 60° = 7.0 m/s. vy0 = 14 sin 60° = 12.124 m/s. The roof is above the hand, so y = +6.0 m.
6.0 = 12.124t + ½(−9.8)t², so 4.9t² − 12.124t + 6.0 = 0.
t = [12.124 ± √(12.124² − 4(4.9)(6.0))] / 9.8 = (12.124 ± 5.421) / 9.8, so t = 0.684 s or 1.790 s.
The box passes roof height on the way up at 0.684 s and lands on the way down, so t = 1.790 s, which is 1.8 s.
x = vx·t = (7.0)(1.790) = 12.53 m, which is 13 m.
questions.finalAnswer: t = 1.8 s (1.79 s, the later root)   x = 13 m (12.5 m)

steps.note: that is roof height on the way up; it lands on the way down

questions.prompt: Shrek and Donkey borrow a trebuchet and fling a giant onion at 28 m/s, 40° above the horizontal, from the top of a 15 m castle wall. It lands on the level field below. Ogres have layers, and so does this problem.
parts: (a) Find the onion's maximum height above the field.
(b) Find its time in the air.
(c) Find how far from the base of the wall it lands.
questions.solution:
vx = 28 cos 40° = 21.45 m/s. vy0 = 28 sin 40° = 18.00 m/s.
(a) At the top vy = 0: 0 = vy0² + 2gy, so y = (18.00)² / 2(9.8) = 16.53 m above the wall top. Add the wall: 16.53 + 15 = 31.53 m, which is 32 m above the field.
(b) The field is 15 m below the launch: −15 = 18.00t + ½(−9.8)t², so 4.9t² − 18.00t − 15 = 0. t = [18.00 + √(18.00² + 4(4.9)(15))] / 9.8 = (18.00 + 24.86) / 9.8 = 4.37 s, which is 4.4 s. The other root is negative.
(c) x = vx·t = (21.45)(4.37) = 93.7 m, which is 94 m.
questions.finalAnswer: (a) 32 m above the field (31.5 m)   (b) 4.4 s (4.37 s)   (c) 94 m (93.7 m)

steps.note: above the top of the wall
that is above the wall, not the field

questions.prompt: Ash throws a Poké Ball at 18 m/s, 20° below the horizontal, from a cliff 35 m above a lake where a Gyarados is waiting. Pikachu declined to throw it for him.
parts: (a) Find the time the ball takes to reach the water.
(b) Find how far from the base of the cliff it lands.
(c) Find the ball's velocity as it hits the water: speed and angle below the horizontal.
questions.solution:
vx = 18 cos 20° = 16.91 m/s. Thrown below the horizontal, so vy0 = −18 sin 20° = −6.16 m/s. The water is 35 m below, so y = −35 m.
(a) −35 = −6.16t + ½(−9.8)t², so 4.9t² + 6.16t − 35 = 0. t = [−6.16 + √(6.16² + 4(4.9)(35))] / 9.8 = (−6.16 + 26.91) / 9.8 = 2.117 s, which is 2.1 s. The other root is negative.
(b) x = vx·t = (16.91)(2.117) = 35.8 m, which is 36 m.
(c) vy = vy0 + gt = −6.16 + (−9.8)(2.117) = −26.91 m/s. vx is still 16.91 m/s. Rebuild the vector (S2.2): v = √(16.91² + 26.91²) = 31.78 m/s, which is 32 m/s. Angle = inverse tan of (26.91 / 16.91) = 57.9°, which is 58° below the horizontal. (Unrounded components give 57.84°, also 58°.)
questions.finalAnswer: (a) 2.1 s (2.12 s)   (b) 36 m (35.8 m)   (c) 32 m/s at 58° below the horizontal

steps.note: thrown below the horizontal, so v_{y0} is negative

equations.note: components; vy0 is negative for a launch below the horizontal
equations.plain: vx = v cos(angle)     vy0 = v sin(angle)
y = vy0 · t + ½ g t²

equations.note: quadratic formula, for at² + bt + c = 0
